attributes.name: smolFire — Lower-bound Runtime, Temporal Storage & Lineage

definition.text:
# smolFire: lower-bound runtime, temporal storage, and lineage

Canonical source (ryanmaclean/smolfire, renamed from smolbsd): `docs/LOWER-BOUND-RUNTIME-2026-09-23.md`

## Objective

Find the smallest/fastest permissively licensed runtime that can run agent work while avoiding duplicated state logic across filesystem, queue, database, tracing, lineage, and orchestration.

## Current execution candidates

- FreeBSD smolFire one-ELF PVH microVM: measured reference. ~37 MiB ELF; 511 ms to shell under Firecracker (569 ms QEMU microvm) in the 2026-07-29 validation run 30409991192; on the same hosted runner the release wall-clock median was 476 ms before and 240 ms after the guest-side TSC-from-pvclock patch (2026-09-24, run 35956015747; n=3, AMD EPYC 9V74; part of the drop is a faster host, the patch's own saving is ~250 ms of thread0). Remaining: console output, phantom UARTs, lapic clockcalib (docs/BOOT-TIME-ROADMAP.md).
- NetBSD 11 MICROVM: smallest complete NetBSD candidate. Host-side prototype runner exists (bin/netbsd-microvm-prototype.nu, docs/NETBSD-MICROVM-PROTOTYPE.md); the LFS workload marker in that doc is a contract example, not a measurement.
- NetBSD rump / rumprun: software lower bound before hardware. Prototype contract and comparison checked in (docs/RUMP-RUMPRUN-LOWER-BOUND.md, docs/lower-bound-rump-rumprun.json), FFS first.
- FPGA / SmartNIC / DPU / NVMe transaction sequencer: hardware lower bound

## Storage matrix

- HAMMER1: native fine-grained transaction history
- HAMMER2: modern portable BSD filesystem candidate
- NetBSD LFS: append/log/checkpoint semantics
- NetBSD FFS + WAPBL + fss: mature correctness baseline

Common workload: create card → pending/running rename → append logs → write artifact → done/failed → fsync → crash → recover → reconstruct history → export lineage.

## Lineage rule

BOP + filesystem-native identities are canonical. OpenLineage is derived.

- card/template → Job
- execution/lease UUID → Run
- HAMMER TID / LFS checkpoint / HAMMER2 snapshot/PFS / FFS snapshot → DatasetVersion
- state rename → START/COMPLETE/FAIL

No second canonical lineage DB.

## Jev / System One

Use only as a fast decision plane:

- provider selection/rotation
- retry/fail/escalate
- priority/routing
- capability match
- review/tool gates
- choose deterministic vs expensive LLM path

Do not use for code/text generation. Safety invariants remain deterministic.

## Shipped release reference (0.5.0, 2026-09-24)

- amd64 VM image: 62.6 MiB raw / 25.0 MiB compressed, 9 s to login on KVM
- aarch64 VM image: 24.2 MiB compressed, 30-31 s to login under same-ISA TCG soft-gate (no hosted runner can hardware-accelerate an aarch64 guest)
- Host-bench of shipped bytes under TCG: amd64 43 s to login; aarch64 cross-ISA 82 s
- These are VM-image figures; the one-ELF SMOLFIRE microVM is the separate row above.

## Hardware direction

Prototype one transaction primitive:

mutation descriptor → sequence/TID → timestamp → hash/checksum → route → DMA/NVMe append → completion.

Measure a software ring first, then FPGA/SmartNIC/DPU.

## Open work

smolFire (ryanmaclean/smolfire) #60, #61, #62, #63, #64, #65, #72, #73; umbrella #78. Status as of 2026-10-03 not verified for each (issue states unreachable in the audit session except #76: closed not_planned 2026-09-24).
BOP ryanmaclean/bop#5, #7
